subject: pe
title: The Cardiovascular Engine
welcome_lead: Heart, vessels and blood — keep oxygen moving to working muscles.
meta_desc: A-Level PE adventure on cardiac output, Frank-Starling law and cardiovascular response.
final_note: Q = HR × SV — the simplest equation in exercise physiology controls everything.

concepts.def: Volume of blood pumped per minute: Q = HR × SV (L min⁻¹).
Beats per minute; ~70 at rest, ~200 at max in young adults.
Volume pumped per beat; ~70 mL at rest, ~120 mL in trained athletes.
Increased venous return → increased SV via stretch of cardiac muscle.
Blood returning to right atrium; aided by muscle and respiratory pumps.
Redirection of blood from gut to muscles via vasoconstriction/dilation.

walkthroughs.body_html: At rest Q ≈ 5 L min⁻¹; during max exercise it can exceed 30 L min⁻¹ in elite endurance athletes.
Greater end-diastolic volume stretches sarcomeres, increasing force of contraction — boosting SV.
During exercise, sympathetic outflow constricts splanchnic vessels and dilates muscle arterioles, redirecting blood.
